messages:
Lara (PM): Heads up — we need to lock priorities for the Private onboarding work tied to customer-managed networking. Several SOC enterprise prospects asked for 'bring-your-own-network' in the next quarter.
Mike (EngInfra): +1. We should scope minimal viable surface vs full BGP/VPN feature set.
Sophia (NetEng): Quick note: from a tech lift POV, there are 3 distinct asks we keep seeing: 1) static routed peering (IP-level), 2) IPsec/VPN and 3) BGP-based DX/Direct Connect. Each has different acceptance criteria.
Lara (PM): Proposal: ship an initial alpha that supports static routed peering + documented NAT/egress behaviour, then follow up with BGP and managed VPN. Opinions?
Raj (Security): Security constraints: customers require immutable audit trails for route changes + KMS-wrapped certs for any key material. Need to include HSM/KMS integration in acceptance criteria for any launch beyond alpha.
Mike (EngInfra): For alpha we can avoid KMS if we keep keys ephemeral and enforce rotation, but we must document that it's not FIPS/HSM-grade.
Sophia (NetEng): Edge cases: asymmetric routing, MTU mismatches (IPv4 jumbo frames), and hairpin traffic when model runners call back into customer infra. We should call these out in the RFC.
Lara (PM): Sounds good. Let's write an RFC that lists: scope, non-goals, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, test matrix, and fallback behaviours. I can draft the PRD. Who wants to co-author the RFC?
Mike (EngInfra): I can take the implementation section (provisioning flow, idempotency, retries, metrics).
Sophia (NetEng): I'll take network design (route tables, eBPF/iptables implications, MTU, dual-stack IPv6 notes).
Raj (Security): I'll add security and compliance requirements (audit logs, KMS, access controls, threat model).
Lara (PM): Great. Draft outline I want in the RFC:
- Background/customer asks (3 example customers)
- Target alpha scope (static routed peering, documented NAT/Egress IP behaviour)
- Acceptance criteria for alpha:
  * Automated provisioning from Console/CLI in <30m for standard configs
  * End-to-end data path sanity: Nagle/MTU test and packet echo success >99%
  * Clear documented security caveat: no KMS-backed certs in alpha
  * Telemetry: per-tenant egress IPs and bytes/s tokenized in Console
- Non-goals (BGP, managed HSM)
- Rollout: canary -> customer opt-in -> GA
- Rollback: automatic fallback to Hosted routing if mismatch or >5% packet loss

Mike (EngInfra): Suggest we add performance SLOs: p99 control-plane latency < 10s for provisioning, and no per-request latency regression >5% for plant-exchange calls.
Sophia (NetEng): Also add validation hooks: we should run an automated connectivity checker that verifies bidirectional flows and validates route propagation. Provide sample check output, e.g.:
```
CHECK: tunnel-up=true; icmp_loss=0%; mtu=1500
ROUTE: 10.40.0.0/24 -> peer-10.0.0.5 (static)
```
Lara (PM): Nice. For launch criteria we need at least one customer reference that ran a full integration in staging and signed off on: provisioning, failover, and audit logs.
Raj (Security): We also require a threat-model review and pen-test signoff for GA. For alpha, a light threat model doc is sufficient.
Mike (EngInfra): Dependency list: console changes, infra installer (on-prem agent), routing agent, telemetry pipeline, and runbook. Lead times: installer changes ~3 weeks, routing agent ~4 weeks, console ~2 weeks.
Lara (PM): Prioritization ask: if we have to cut scope, cut console polish and keep CLI + API for alpha. Customers can use API scripts for onboarding.
Sophia (NetEng): Edge-case to call out: overlapping CIDRs. We must either require unique CIDR or implement SNAT for overlapping ranges. SNAT will add complexity and performance costs. Recommend unique CIDR as alpha requirement.
Mike (EngInfra): Agree. Make overlapping CIDR support a post-alpha feature.
Lara (PM): Action items: 
- Lara: draft RFC + PRD (due in 4 business days)
- Mike: write provisioning flow + idempotency notes (due in 6 days)
- Sophia: design doc for routing + validation hooks (due in 6 days)
- Raj: security checklist + threat-model stub (due in 6 days)
- All: review RFC in #eng-platform once posted, aim for RFC review within 72h of posting.

Deploy Bot: deploy-checklist created: /deploy/checks/private-networking-alpha, items=7

Lara (PM): One more thing — customers asked for clear fallthrough behavior when Private routes fail (should traffic go to hosted fallback or drop?). Preference from sales: fallback to hosted for availability. Need engineering feedback.
Mike (EngInfra): Fallback to hosted is possible but we must be explicit about data plane boundaries and data residency implications. Document as opt-in per customer.
Raj (Security): If fallback goes to hosted, that has compliance implications. Must be opt-in and logged per-tenant. Also require customer consent in TOS.
Sophia (NetEng): Implementation note: fallback path needs sticky egress IP and consistent routing to avoid session breakage. That requires stateful mapping in our routing agent.
Lara (PM): Ok — include fallback as opt-in GA-only feature. Alpha: no automatic fallback; manual failover only.
Mike (EngInfra): I'll prototype a sticky-eip mapping in a feature branch next week.
Lara (PM): Thanks team. I'll post the RFC draft later today. Please add any small items as replies to this thread so I can incorporate them before I publish.
Sophia (NetEng): Added one more: IPv6 dual-stack customers — alpha should be IPv4-only, note IPv6 as roadmap item.
Raj (Security): Logging retention: customers expect 1 year for audit trails for some industries. Add retention config to GA checklist.
Lara (PM): Noted. Closing the thread for now; I'll ping again when RFC is posted. :thumbsup:
